topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: The soft, familiar fur brushes against my fingers, a sudden warmth in the cool air. The eyes, once bright and unyielding, now faint and clouded, stare back at me. It’s the scent that truly reaches me, a faded echo of days long buried under the weight of years. This thing, so small yet vast with the weight of time, rests in my hands. The world around me fades, the chatter of the yard sale, the rustle of leaves, all mute against the rush of memories this bear brings to the surface. I hold it tightly, fingers tracing the worn seams, the frayed edges a map of journeys traveled and forgotten.
